subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw status falsely reports openclaw-mem0 memory as unavailable when the live gateway plugin is working

question: Should memory status/doctor reporting use live gateway memory-runtime health as the source of truth for external memory plugins, or is the current `not checked` and local-manager behavior sufficient?
rationale: Current main softened the false-negative wording but did not implement the live-runtime health contract requested here, and the broader open issue plus conflicting fork PR require a maintainer-owned boundary choice.

options.title: Use the live-gateway contract
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 the canonical implementation path, close or replace the conflicting fork PR, and require live external-memory proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Revive the fork PR
options.body: Ask the fork PR author to rebase, resolve conflicts, and prove `status --deep` plus JSON status against a real external memory plugin without local startup side effects.

options.title: Accept current wording
options.body: Declare `not checked` sufficient for normal/deep status, close the conflicting fork PR, and close this issue only with explicit maintainer rationale.

recommendation.title: Use the live-gateway contract
recommendation.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 the canonical implementation path, close or replace the conflicting fork PR, and require live external-memory proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest history signal on the memory-runtime plugin routing and status boundary, which is the product decision this issue now needs.
